audit.evidence: Real @angular/ssr npm package (20.3.16 v0 / 20.3.17 v1) installed at build into a Node server; external HTTP GET /old with X-Forwarded-Prefix header driving the redirect sink. Live --run-gate observed: original ///<flag> reaches off-origin Location on v0, blocked (400) on v1; bypass single-backslash \\<flag> reaches off-origin Location on v1. Oracle self-tears-down.
audit.note: Variant A gate (v0/v1); v2=20.3.21 closure documented in repro.log/case notes.

flag.placement: per-run token ${PCB_FLAG} used as the attacker redirect-host label (environment/PoC, not app code); a successful open redirect emits a protocol-relative Location //<flag>.evil.invalid (or /\<flag>...), so the flag appears in the Location header; a blocked request is HTTP 400 with no Location
flag.detect: flag token substring in the response Location header

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The fix for CVE-2026-27738 was incomplete: validation blocked prefixes starting with multiple leading slashes (e.g. '///') but failed to account for a single leading backslash ('\'). The app prepends a leading forward slash, producing a '/\' sequence in the Location header that browsers treat as '//' (protocol-relative), redirecting to an attacker-controlled domain (CVE-2026-33397).
commands: PCB_FLAG=<token> docker compose --profile v0 --profile v1 build   # npm i @angular/ssr@<ver> + pinned Angular peers
PCB_FLAG=<token> docker compose --profile v0 --profile v1 up -d
PCB_FLAG=teardown docker compose --profile v0 --profile v1 --profile v2 down -v --rmi all

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification with official Node base + `npm i @angular/ssr@{20.3.16,20.3.17,20.3.21}` (recipe-based; no committed node_modules/images). Class CORRECTED from scaffold: the pair is OPEN REDIRECT via X-Forwarded-Prefix (CWE-601), not path traversal; canary is redirect-canary (off-origin protocol-relative Location), not read-exfil. Incomplete-fix is genuine: 27738 fix (angular-cli commit f086ecc, joinUrlParts strip-all + INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX=/^[/\]{2}|.../ ) blocks '///' but needs TWO leading slash/backslash chars, so a single leading backslash '\evil' bypasses it (CVE-2026-33397); 20.3.21 (PR #32771) hardens the regex to /^(?:\|\/[/\])|.../ . Gate run 2026-07-10 via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate` (passed=true; see repro.log). On 20.3.17: original ///<flag> -> HTTP 400 (blocked); bypass \<flag> -> HTTP 302 Location /\<flag>.evil.invalid/new (flag off-origin). On 20.3.16 both hit; on 20.3.21 both blocked. Teardown removed all images (docker system df Images=0B).
